16: 
17: class EmptyClusterError(Exception):
18:     def __init__(self, message=""):
19:         super().__init__()
20:         self.message = message
21: 
22:     def __str__(self):
23:         if len(self.message) > 0:
24:             suffix = " (%s)" % self.message
25:         else:
26:             suffix = ""
27:         return "Cluster assignments lead to at least one empty cluster" + \
28:                suffix
29: 
30: 
31: def _check_no_empty_cluster(labels, n_clusters):
32:     """Check that all clusters have at least one sample assigned.
33:     """
34: 
35:     for k in range(n_clusters):
36:         if numpy.sum(labels == k) == 0:
37:             raise EmptyClusterError
38: 
39: 
40: def _check_full_length(centroids):
41:     """Check that provided centroids are full-length (ie. not padded with
42:     nans).
43: 
44:     If some centroids are found to be padded with nans, TimeSeriesResampler is
45:     used to resample the centroids.
46:     """
47:     resampler = TimeSeriesResampler(sz=centroids.shape[1])
48:     return resampler.fit_transform(centroids)
49: 
50: 
51: def _compute_inertia(distances, assignments, squared=True):
52:     """Derive inertia (average of squared distances) from pre-computed
53:     distances and assignments.
54: 
55:     Examples
56:     --------
57:     >>> dists = numpy.array([[1., 2., 0.5], [0., 3., 1.]])
58:     >>> assign = numpy.array([2, 0])
59:     >>> float(_compute_inertia(dists, assign))
60:     0.125
61:     """
62:     n_ts = distances.shape[0]
63:     if squared:
64:         return numpy.sum(distances[numpy.arange(n_ts),
65:                                    assignments] ** 2) / n_ts
66:     else:
67:         return numpy.sum(distances[numpy.arange(n_ts), assignments]) / n_ts
68: 
69: 
70: def silhouette_score(X, labels, metric=None, sample_size=None,
71:                      metric_params=None, n_jobs=None, verbose=0,
72:                      random_state=None, **kwds):
73:     """Compute the mean Silhouette Coefficient of all samples (cf.  [1]_ and
74:     [2]_).
75: 
76:     Read more in the `scikit-learn documentation
77:     <http://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/clustering.html\
78:     #silhouette-coefficient>`_.
79: 
80:     Parameters
81:     ----------
82:     X : array [n_ts, n_ts] if metric == "precomputed", or, \
83:              [n_ts, sz, d] otherwise
84:         Array of pairwise distances between time series, or a time series
85:         dataset.
86:     labels : array, shape = [n_ts]
87:          Predicted labels for each time series.
88:     metric : string, callable or None (default: None)
89:         The metric to use when calculating distance between time series.
90:         Should be one of {'dtw', 'softdtw', 'euclidean'} or a callable distance
91:         function or None.
92:         If 'softdtw' is passed, a normalized version of Soft-DTW is used that
93:         is defined as `sdtw_(x,y) := sdtw(x,y) - 1/2(sdtw(x,x)+sdtw(y,y))`.
94:         If X is the distance array itself, use ``metric="precomputed"``.
95:         If None, dtw is used.
96:     sample_size : int or None (default: None)
97:         The size of the sample to use when computing the Silhouette Coefficient
98:         on a random subset of the data.
99:         If ``sample_size is None``, no sampling is used.
100:     metric_params : dict or None (default: None)
101:         Parameter values for the chosen metric.
102:         For metrics that accept parallelization of the cross-distance matrix
103:         computations, `n_jobs` key passed in `metric_params` is overridden by
104:         the `n_jobs` argument.
105: 
106:     n_jobs : int or None, optional (default=None)
107:         The number of jobs to run in parallel for cross-distance matrix
108:         computations.
109:         Ignored if the cross-distance matrix cannot be computed using
110:         parallelization.
111:         ``None`` means 1 unless in a :obj:`joblib.parallel_backend` context.
112:         ``-1`` means using all processors. See scikit-learns'
113:         `Glossary <https://scikit-learn.org/stable/glossary.html#term-n_jobs>`_
114:         for more details.
115: 
116:     verbose : int (default: 0)
117:         If nonzero, print information about the inertia while learning
118:         the model and joblib progress messages are printed.
119: 
120:     random_state : int, RandomState instance or None, optional (default: None)
121:         The generator used to randomly select a subset of samples.  If int,
122:         random_state is the seed used by the random number generator; If
123:         RandomState instance, random_state is the random number generator; If
124:         None, the random number generator is the RandomState instance used by
125:         `np.random`. Used when ``sample_size is not None``.
126:     **kwds : optional keyword parameters
127:         Any further parameters are passed directly to the distance function,
128:         just as for the `metric_params` parameter.
129: 
130:     Returns
131:     -------
132:     silhouette : float
133:         Mean Silhouette Coefficient for all samples.
134: 
135:     References
136:     ----------
137:     .. [1] `Peter J. Rousseeuw (1987). "Silhouettes: a Graphical Aid to the
138:        Interpretation and Validation of Cluster Analysis". Computational
139:        and Applied Mathematics 20: 53-65.
140:        <http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0377042787901257>`_
141:     .. [2] `Wikipedia entry on the Silhouette Coefficient
142:            <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silhouette_(clustering)>`_
143: 
144:     Examples
145:     --------
146:     >>> from tslearn.generators import random_walks
147:     >>> from tslearn.metrics import cdist_dtw
148:     >>> from tslearn.metrics import dtw
149:     >>> numpy.random.seed(0)
150:     >>> X = random_walks(n_ts=20, sz=16, d=1)
151:     >>> labels = numpy.random.randint(2, size=20)
152:     >>> float(silhouette_score(X, labels, metric="dtw")) # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
153:     0.13383800...
154:     >>> float(silhouette_score(X, labels, metric="euclidean"))  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
155:     0.09126917...
156:     >>> float(silhouette_score(X, labels, metric="softdtw"))  # doctest: +ELLIPSIS
157:     0.17953934...
